x: Ron Jeal managed one or two good throws but was rather inconsistent and does not seem to be able to recapture the form which enabled him to win the Surrey Championship two or three years ago.
The past season, in spite of a further reduction in active members, has been very successful. Ron Jeal, Charlie Melchoir, George Powell, Bill Sutton, a promising new member, L.
Patience, Bill Sutton and Ben May, to all of whom we offer our congratulations.—What a team for 1962! We are also pleased to hear that Ron Jeal has become the father of a daughter.—Congrats.
Charlie Melchior and Ron Jeal finished first and second in the Javelin event, and the former has been throwing in consistent style throughout the season.

Ron Jeal also has not been able to turn out until the last few matches. We have been glad to welcome a new member in the person [illegible] Pat Ridge of the Irish Guards, whose shot putting and discus throwing are first class and have been extremely useful in gaining us first places in several matches.
Ron Jeal, now evacuated to Streatford, Lancs., writes: "What a link the old Mag is." Len Marchant has joined the noble order of benedicts.

Unfortunately, we shall not have the services of Ron Jeal in the Javelin. He has been transferred and will be doing his stuff with the Manchester A.C. of which club he has become a second-claim member.

The Surrey Championships saw Ron Jeal gain second place in the Javelin with Charlie Jones third. Our Field Events Captain also gained second place in the Hop, Step and Jump with an effort of 39 feet, 8¾ inches.

At the Surrey County Championships our members did well, and Len Marchant was third in the 880, while Len Herbert annexed the 3 Mile title. Jimmy Wood, a second-claim member, won the 1 Mile, and in the Senior Javelin, Ron Jeal was second and Charlie Jones third.

Ron Jeal, although now stationed with the R.A.F. in the South has, unfortunately, not been able to turn out, but we hope he will by next season, and show a return to his 1937-38 form, in which he produced throws of over 170 feet.
